Ezekiel

Introduction

Isikil (was a) sacrificer long_ago there in Hirusalim and he (was) one of (those) captured(pl) that was_taken(pl) there to Babilunya before Hirusalim was_snatched, until it was_snatched in the year 586, before Kristu was_born. Therefore he lived there in Babilunya and he became a prophet in the fifth years from his being_captured. His message (was) for those people who were captured that are already there in Babilunya and those there in Hirusalim. The document by Isikil is_divided into six: 1/ The calling of Isikil by God as a prophet; 2/ The warnings there to the people concerning the punishment of God for_them, and of the coming demolition of Hirusalim; 3/ the words of God concerning the punishment that he will_make_ the nations that oppressed and taught the (ones) from_Israilita to sin _experience; 4/ the comforting for Israil when the enemies snatched Hirusalim, and the promise concerning the arrival of good living; 5/ the defeat of all Israil enemies; 6/ the illustrating by Isikil of the temple and the nation that returned to it's former situation/welfare.

The faith/believing of Isikil (was) big, and his thinking (was) very_good (LIT moving_fast and far). Most of his thoughts, came by_means of being_revealed. And most of his words/messages, were_shown by_means of action(s) that had meaning, and this was_seen by all. Isikil showed the importance of having_a_new heart and spirit, and the necessity of every person to_turn_his_back on his/her own sin. Isikil also storied concerning Israil hoping for a new living. And as prophet and sacrificer, he had big encouragement for the temple, and the needs in_order to_be_holy.

From the east to the west, the length is twelve (12) kilometers, and the width is five kilometers from the north side to the south side. And there in the middle of that land where the temple will_be_built. 11 That holy land, will_be given to the sacrificer the descendants of Saduk who were on_the_contrary faithful in serving me and did not leave me. Not like what some Libita did who followed the Israilitas who left me. 12 That is the very holy land, and right gift for the sacrificers who were the descendants of Saduk. 13 It is alongside the land of some Libita in which the length is twelve (12) kilometers and the width is five kilometers. 14 They should not sell it or exchange even just a small part of it because it's already set_apart for the Lord.

15 And the portion of the land which is twelve (12) kilometers lenght and the width is two and a half kilometers, that's where all the people can live and the pastures of the animals. 16 And the city will be in the midst and equal_in_size and the length and width is two kilometers (each). 17 And the city will_be_encircled with the courtyard in which the width and the length is 125 meters (both). 18 And the remaining portion which is in the opposite of the outside of the city, there_is a field which is five kilometers in length on east (side), and also five kilometers to the west (side). The crops of that field will_be the foods for the workers of the city. 19 The inhabitants of the city are the workers of that field (they) are all from the tribe of Israil. 20 Therefore the width and the length should be equal_in_size twelve (12) kilometers the entire land that will_set_apart for the Lord, including the holy land and the city.

21 The remaining portion of the land which opposite_of_each in both sides of the holy land and city, will_be_possessed by the leader. From the holy land to the boundary on east side and to the boundary on west side. 22 The holy land, the temple, the land of Libita and the city will be in the midst of the land of the leader. And the land of the leader which opposite_to_each_other will_ also _be in the midst of the land of the descendants of Huda and Binhamin.

23 And these are also the land that other tribes will_possess. The land of Binhamin, is on the north side of the land of the leader. Its width, is from the east to the west side of the land of Israil. 24 And there in the south (LIT right_side) of the land of the descendants of Binhamin, is the land of the descendants of Simyun. The width of that, is also from the east towards the west of the part of the land of Israil. 25-27 And the next land, are the land of the descendants of Isakar, Sabulun, and Gad. And the width of that, is also from the east towards the west of the part of the land of Israil. 28 And on the south side of the boundary of the land of Gad, which follows Tamar to the creek of Kadis-Miriba, to Ihiptu till the Sea of Mediterranean.

29 That's the land the tribe of Israil will_possess as their inheritance. I (am) the Lord the (one who) is_saying this.

The doorways of the city

30 [xr]And the city has twelve (12) gates. For the four wall around the city, there are three gates each. 31 The gate on the north side, called the Gate of Rubin, Gate of Huda, and the Gate of Libi. 32 And the gate(s) on the east side, are_called the Gate of Husi (Joseph), Gate of Binhamin, and the Gate of Dan. 33 And the gate on the south side, called Gate of Simyun, Gate of Isakar, and the Gate of Sabulun. 34 And the gate on the west side, called the Gate of Gad, Gate of Asir, and the Gate of Naptali. 35 The height of each wall, is 2,250 meters. Therefore there are nine thousand (9,000) meters long for four walls. And from that time on, the city will_be called, “The Lord God is there.”

4:13 The words ‘food that was considered dirty’ mean it was forbidden to be eaten by the Law of Moses (Deu. 14:1-21). If a person ate the food that was considered dirty then that person would also be considered dirty and could not accompany other fellow Israelites in worshipping God. In this verse the food was considered dirty because it was in the nations that were outside of Israel which were considered dirty. See Jos 22:19 and Amo 7:17.
